findings.title: pathTokensInCommand cannot match Windows backslash path tokens; its backslash normalization is unreachable
findings.summary: The token regex character class [\w.@-] excludes backslash and requires at least one forward slash, so a targeted command written with Windows-style paths (e.g. `node scripts\remediate\verify-hosts.mjs` or `npx vitest run tests\x.test.mjs`) yields zero path tokens — the subsequent `t.replace(/\\/g, "/")` normalization can never fire. Consequence: selfContainedVerifyCommands keeps a backslash-authored command that references a sibling node's not-yet-created deliverable (the exact guaranteed-fail cross-node deadlock the function exists to drop, per its own doc), and isDistDependentVerifyCommand's treeRoot content scan silently skips backslash-named test files.
evidence: src/remediate/steps/dispatch/verifyCommands.ts:183 - the match char class [\w.@-] contains no backslash and the group requires a literal '/', so no matched token can ever contain '\'; the .replace(/\\/g, "/") on line 184 is dead code, which shows backslash paths were intended to be handled but are not.

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/verifyCommands.ts:199-213 - selfContainedVerifyCommands iterates pathTokensInCommand(cmd); a command whose only path references are backslash-form produces no tokens and is unconditionally kept, defeating the cross-node self-containment gate documented at lines 187-198.

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/verifyCommands.ts:142-143 - isDistDependentVerifyCommand's content scan also iterates pathTokensInCommand, so a backslash-named .test.mjs that spawns dist/ is not content-scanned (only the literal 'dist' in the command string itself is caught at line 140).

findings.title: Per-chunk Buffer.toString() in onStdout mangles multi-byte UTF-8 characters split across chunk boundaries in progress events
findings.summary: onStdout decodes each raw chunk independently (chunk.toString()) before appending to stdoutLineBuf. A multi-byte UTF-8 code point split across two chunks decodes to U+FFFD replacement characters in the onProgress 'output' lines. The log file is unaffected (raw bytes are written), but consumers of progress messages see corrupted text. A StringDecoder (or a single stream encoding) is the standard fix.
evidence: src/shared/providers/spawnLoggedCommand.ts:269 - each Buffer chunk is decoded in isolation; UTF-8 sequences ending mid-codepoint at a chunk boundary cannot decode correctly this way.
src/shared/providers/spawnLoggedCommand.ts:264 - the writeLog call receives the raw Buffer, so only the progress-event channel (emitOutputLine) is affected.

findings.title: Persistent EPERM/EACCES on lock creation is classified as transient contention and spins until a misattributed timeout
findings.summary: acquireLock treats EPERM/EACCES from the wx create as transient Windows create/delete contention and retries. That is right for the racing case, but a genuinely permission-denied lock directory (ACL change, read-only mount) now spins through the full backoff window and surfaces as FileLockTimeoutError('Timed out acquiring lock'), hiding the real EACCES root cause from the operator and costing the full timeoutMs on every acquisition.

src/shared/quota/fileLock.ts:26 - FileLockTimeoutError carries only the lock path, so the underlying errno is unrecoverable by callers or logs.

findings.title: Positional task-id fallback captures a flag token when flags precede the positional argument
findings.summary: When --task-id is absent, cmdExplainTask falls back to argv[3] verbatim without checking that the token is not a flag. findings.title: Shipped worker schemas under-constrain the acceptance contract: reviewed_clean conditionality is not encoded
findings.summary: The authoritative validator enforces conditional rules the shipped JSON schemas do not express: an empty findings array is only accepted with reviewed_clean:true, reviewed_clean alongside non-empty findings is rejected, and lens_verification results must carry a verification object. In audit_result.schema.json and audit_results.schema.json, reviewed_clean is a plain optional boolean with no if/then coupling to findings, so a worker that self-validates against the schema (the documented optional step) gets a green self-check on a payload the merge will reject.
findings.impact: The schema's advertised purpose in packets is optional pre-submit self-validation; for the empty-findings case (the single most common worker payload shape) it validates exactly the payload the tool rejects, so the self-check gives false confidence precisely where the contract has its hardest rule. Draft 2020-12 can express this with if/then (findings maxItems:0 => required reviewed_clean, const true), so the constraint is encodable at the zod-to-JSON-schema render, not inherently prose-only.
evidence: schemas/audit_result.schema.json:546-554 - required is only ['task_id','unit_id','pass_id','lens','file_coverage','findings']; no conditional keywords (if/then/allOf) appear anywhere in the file.

The dispatch packet prompt states the rule as a hard validation rule ('An empty findings array is only accepted when you also set reviewed_clean: true' and 'Setting reviewed_clean: true alongside one or more findings is also rejected') — enforced by validateAuditResults, invisible to the schema.
schemas/audit_results.schema.json is the same object shape wrapped in an array (minItems 1) with the same gap.

findings.title: src is fully typechecked three times per verify-and-commit cycle with incremental and composite both off, so no typecheck work is ever reused
findings.summary: tsconfig.base.json sets no incremental and no composite, and there are no project references anywhere; tsconfig.test.json re-declares include: ['src','tests'], so it re-parses and re-checks the entire 129k-line src tree from scratch rather than consuming src's emitted declarations. The result is three full passes over src per cycle: check:tests (measured 5,372 ms) and build (measured 5,028 ms) both inside verify:checks, plus the pre-commit gate's own npm run check (tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit) on every commit - and each pass starts cold because nothing is cached (no .tsbuildinfo exists on disk). Turning tsconfig.json into a composite project, referencing it from tsconfig.test.json, and enabling incremental makes the test typecheck consume dist .d.ts instead of re-checking src, and makes repeat runs near-instant on an unchanged tree. This is the standard tsc project-references arrangement, needs no new dependency, and is worth roughly 10 s per verify plus the full cost of the pre-commit check on every commit - the highest-frequency gate in the repo.

findings.title: Suite registry in predictable world-writable temp dir trusts forgeable entries; EPERM-as-alive makes a forged pid-1 holder permanent
findings.summary: The running-suite registry lives at a name any local user can predict (sha256 of the checkout path) inside the world-writable OS temp dir, and entries are trusted from any writer. findings.title: Terminology defects at the centre of the loop: bounded step is defined by retraction in four homes, and obligation names two unrelated lattices with inverted ordering conventions
findings.summary: Two perspectives found two instances of one cheap, high-comprehension-leverage class, so they merge. First, the invariant reads: one bounded step per invocation equals a fold-aware drain, not a single obligation — the term's definition is a retraction of the term. The same correction is restated in docs/project-philosophy.md (A1), again in CLAUDE.md's audit-architecture section, and again in spec/audit/entrypoint-contract.md; fold-aware appears across 9 files including four test names. Any name that needs three sentences of 'this does not mean what it says' has selected the wrong name, and each new home inherits the correction, which is why there are four copies. The underlying behavior takes one clause to state accurately: a call keeps draining deterministic work and stops at the first point it needs you. Bounded step fails because it implies exactly one; fold-aware drain fails because fold is undefined jargon and aware carries no information. Second, the word obligation carries two unrelated meanings: in the engine it is a unit of orchestrator progress (src/shared/engine/obligationEngine.ts, selected by an ordered priority array), while in the contract pipeline it is a derived requirement on a change (src/remediate/steps/contractPipeline.ts:2833 declares a LOCAL type ObligationKind of invariant/behavioral/structural/test, unrelated to the engine type). Both carry an ordering array and the two conventions are inverted: PRIORITY in src/audit/orchestrator/nextStep.ts:25 is highest-priority-first (the scan returns the first actionable entry), while OBLIGATION_KIND_PRIORITY in contractPipeline.ts:2836 is documented as higher index equals higher priority and is consumed via indexOf comparison. A reader who has internalized one convention will misread the other, and the shared word invites exactly that transfer. Recommendation: rename the drain concept to what it does (pause-bounded invocation, or plainly drains-until-it-needs-you) so the retraction has nothing to retract and is deleted from all four homes at once; rename the contract-pipeline concept (RequirementKind / REQUIREMENT_KIND_RANK) and express rank as an explicit numeric field rather than array position in either place, so one ordering convention holds repo-wide.

findings.title: withClaimHeartbeat settles only the LAST tick's heartbeat; an earlier in-flight heartbeat can outlive the guarded call
findings.summary: The teardown guarantee ('Settle any in-flight heartbeat write so none outlives the guarded call') is implemented by awaiting a single `pendingHeartbeat` variable that each interval tick OVERWRITES. If tick N's heartbeat is still pending (e.g. slow withFileLock acquisition under contention, whose backoff reaches 500ms and stale-lock window 30s) when tick N+1 fires, the reference to N's promise is lost and the finally block awaits only N+1. Tick N's registry read-modify-write can then land after the caller has released the claim or begun run-dir teardown — the exact race the tracking comment says this variable exists to prevent. Impact is bounded (heartbeat is token-checked, so a post-release write no-ops), but the residual lock-file create/IO can still race directory teardown and the stated invariant does not hold.
findings.impact: A straggler heartbeat's withFileLock IO (lock-file creation, registry read) can fire against a directory the caller is tearing down; on Windows this is an EBUSY/EPERM flake source. Fix direction: chain (pendingHeartbeat = pendingHeartbeat.then(...)) or collect unsettled promises.
evidence: src/shared/quota/claimLease.ts:81-94 - each tick reassigns pendingHeartbeat, discarding any still-pending prior promise instead of chaining or collecting it.

src/shared/quota/claimLease.ts:100-103 - the finally block awaits only the latest assignment, so the comment 'so none outlives the guarded call' is not guaranteed when heartbeat latency exceeds intervalMs.

findings.summary: The covering tests (tests/audit/dispatch-scripts.test.ts spawns the scripts as child processes; tests/audit/dispatch-validate.test.ts imports dispatch/validate.mjs directly) reach the validation logic only through the scripts' dist imports — validate.mjs loads dist/audit/validation/auditResults.js and merge-results.mjs loads dist/audit/io/runArtifacts.js. `npm test` rebuilds first, but the documented single-file invocation (`npx vitest run tests/audit/<file>.test.ts`) does not, so after editing src/audit/validation these tests verify the previous build's behavior and can pass (or fail) against code that no longer exists in src.
findings.impact: A contributor iterating on the validator with single-file vitest gets green/red verdicts bound to the last `npm run build`, not the source — the exact 'silently pass on stale builds' class this lens names, and a shape this repo has been bitten by before (stale-binary/stale-dist traps are recorded project memory).
evidence: dispatch/validate.mjs:1 and dispatch/merge-results.mjs:4 - the only path from these scripts to the validation/contract logic is through dist/, unavoidable for shipped runtime scripts but inherited by every test that drives them.

tests/audit/dispatch-scripts.test.ts:14-23 - tests spawn the scripts with process.execPath, so vitest's TS transform never touches the logic under test; freshness depends entirely on an out-of-band build step.

findings.title: disposition_overrides prefix matching is ad-hoc and inconsistent with the shared pathMatchesPrefix used for excluded_scope
findings.summary: runPlanningExecutor applies intent_checkpoint.disposition_overrides with a hand-rolled exact/startsWith(override.path + "/") check, while the sibling intent scope field excluded_scope is applied through the shared pathMatchesPrefix helper (scope.ts). An override path written with a trailing slash ('src/vendor/') or with backslash separators never matches any POSIX manifest path under the ad-hoc check, so the override is silently ignored — the same input shape that excluded_scope handles via the shared helper.
evidence: src/audit/orchestrator/planningExecutors.ts:138-143 - disposition_overrides matched with `f.path === override.path || f.path.startsWith(override.path + "/")`; a trailing-slash override yields the prefix 'src/vendor//' which matches nothing, and backslash-separated override paths never match POSIX manifest paths.

src/audit/orchestrator/scope.ts:331 - the adjacent intent-scope mechanism (excluded_scope) routes the same kind of operator-supplied path prefix through the shared pathMatchesPrefix, so the two intent scope fields accept different path spellings.
runtime:unit:src-audit: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test

findings.title: Document-phase dispatch results are validated with the implement-only worker-result validator
findings.summary: validateDispatchArtifacts runs validateImplementWorkerResult over every result file referenced by ANY dispatch plan, including plans whose phase is 'document' (a phase validateDispatchPlan still explicitly accepts and the DispatchPhase type still declares). validateImplementWorkerResult hard-requires phase === 'implement' and the implement contract_version, so any document-phase result file would be flagged with spurious errors. Latent while the dissolved document phase produces no plans, but the validator and the type both still admit the phase, so the mismatch is reachable by contract.
evidence: src/remediate/validation/artifacts.ts:293-298 - the result loop keys referencedResults by phase but then validates every existing result with the implement validator regardless of that phase.

src/remediate/validation/artifacts.ts:143-149 - validateDispatchPlan accepts phase "document" as valid (and enforces finding_id for it at line 188-190), so a document plan is not itself rejected; only its results would be misvalidated.
CLAUDE.md records the document phase as dissolved (N-R13); the retained enum value plus this unconditional implement-validation is the residue.

findings.title: Drift-guard test pins the same worker-writes-result_path contract prose in two independent prompt renderers
findings.summary: This contract test exists to keep two separately-authored prompt texts — renderRollingDispatchPrompt (step prompt, src/audit/cli/prompts.ts) and buildPacketPrompt (worker packet prompt, src/audit/cli/dispatch.ts) — agreeing that the worker WRITES its AuditResult[] to result_path, via regex pins on both renderings. The real defect it polices is that the load-bearing contract sentence is duplicated across two renderers; extracting the contract statement (or at least the shared sentence/fragment) to one shared source consumed by both renderers would make the cross-renderer agreement structural rather than regex-guarded, and the test could shrink to covering the single source.

findings.title: eslint result path relativization uses first-occurrence string replace and is case-sensitive, mis-stripping on Windows
findings.summary: runEslint strips the repo root from eslint's absolute filePath with String.replace(root + "/", "") — a first-occurrence substring replace, not an anchored prefix strip. On Windows, drive-letter casing routinely differs between the configured root and eslint's reported paths (C:/ vs c:/), in which case nothing is stripped and the artifact records absolute paths that will not join with repo-relative paths elsewhere; and if the root string happens to appear mid-path, the wrong span is removed.

findings.title: extractResetsAtClockMs mis-parses duration phrasings and meridiem-less times as clock times
findings.summary: The clock-time reset parser's doc contract says it 'returns null when absent/ambiguous', but the regex accepts an hour with no am/pm and no colon. Text like 'quota resets 3 hours from now' (not matched by the 'Resets in Xh' duration parser, which requires the literal 'Resets in') matches as hour=3 and is interpreted as 03:00 next occurrence; a meridiem-less 'resets 3:30' is silently read as 03:30 (24h), up to ~12h off the real reset. The result feeds cooldown_until, so a mis-parse pauses a pool far longer (or shorter) than the provider stated.
evidence: src/shared/quota/errorParsing.ts:347-364 - both the minutes group and the meridiem group are optional, so a bare 'resets 3' (as in 'resets 3 hours from now') parses as hour 3, minute 0, no meridiem, and is treated as a 24h clock time; the doc comment above claims ambiguous input returns null.

src/shared/quota/errorParsing.ts:336-345 - extractResetsInMs only matches the literal 'Resets in (\d+)h...' shape, so natural duration phrasings fall through to the clock parser instead of being rejected.
src/shared/quota/errorParsing.ts:402-411 - the mis-parsed value becomes retryAfterMs for any USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS match and flows into computeCooldownUntil / HostSessionQuotaSource cooldowns.

findings.title: git helpers parse --name-only output without disabling core.quotepath: non-ASCII paths come back C-quoted and never match the repo's real path spellings

findings.title: isDirectCliExecution path-identity mismatch makes a direct invocation a silent successful no-op
findings.summary: The direct-execution guard compares resolve(argv[1]) string-equal to fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) with no realpath or case normalization. On win32 a caller-supplied path with different drive-letter/path casing, or an invocation through a symlink/junction (Node ESM resolves import.meta.url to the realpath while argv[1] keeps the link path), fails the comparison — the module loads, runs nothing, and the process exits 0. findings.title: Transient snapshot-read failure is latched as a permanent, fully silent degrade for the process lifetime

findings.title: What is genuinely right — the mechanically-enforced primitives and the degenerate-case pattern are the template every finding above should be closed against
findings.summary: All five perspectives independently ended on this note, which is itself evidence: the fundamental approach is sound and the gaps are places it has not yet been applied. This finding merges their credit lists because it changes what the other 44 are asking for — apply your own proven pattern consistently, not rebuild. (1) Enforcement rather than instruction, where it exists, is genuinely hard to fool: quote grounding re-reads a verbatim span from disk and content-matches it, whitespace/CRLF-normalized and matched on content NOT line numbers, so later edits do not false-fail a still-valid quote (src/shared/validation/findingGrounding.ts:158-193) — DR-007 argues only that the property it establishes is weaker than the product claims, not that the mechanism is wrong. The autonomous approval gate is fail-closed by construction: a CLOSED positive enumeration of four provably-safe change kinds, anything unclassifiable excluded, no severity/cost escape hatch, no durable rejection (src/remediate/review/autonomousGate.ts:26-70). The read-only command allowlist is real default-deny with per-executable flag policies, an enumerated read-only git subcommand set, no shell, a 60s timeout with SIGKILL escalation and 256 KiB output cap (src/shared/tooling/allowlistedExec.ts) — DR-001(c) is a one-line hole in an otherwise correct design. Termination is engineered, not hoped for: MAX_DRAIN_STEPS is a graceful stop explicitly coupled to the engine's throwing backstop at +2 so the graceful cap always trips first however the constant is retuned (src/audit/orchestrator/advance.ts:42-48). Cost is bounded by construction: frontier expansion halts at a file budget, skips high-fan-in hubs, drops low-confidence edges, and is deterministic (src/audit/orchestrator/scope.ts:40-52). And knipGraphCrosscheck refuses to promote a dead-code lead to a verdict when the relevant analyzer did not run (:137-139) — exactly the fidelity instinct DR-016 asks the report to inherit. (2) The degenerate-case pattern is the shape to generalize: src/shared/dispatch/unifiedRolling.ts embeds audit as the READ-ONLY degenerate case — one level of read-only nodes that the sub-wave machinery collapses to a no-op — and that degenerate case costs nothing: no second code path, no parity test, no memo. src/shared/fileIntegrity.ts is a genuine higher-order core parameterized by record accessors, so the audit and remediate sides are different INPUTS to one algorithm rather than two implementations. src/audit/orchestrator/dependencyMap.ts derives the forward view by inverting the single hand-authored adjacency so the two can never drift, and constrains its keys to a type derived from ARTIFACT_DEFINITIONS so a stale filename is a compile error. (3) The acquire-and-normalize instinct, where applied, is better than what a reviewer would have recommended: JSON Schema is GENERATED from zod rather than hand-maintained, with a drift test on the committed artifacts; the TOML and YAML parsers use vetted libraries and each carries a docstring recording the bug class its hand-rolled predecessor had; the JS/TS graph layer uses the real TypeScript Compiler API resolved from the AUDITED repo's own typescript first and degrades to a regex floor with confidence encoding the difference; gitignore semantics are deliberately NOT reimplemented (one batched git check-ignore); undici is chosen with the rationale written down at the point of use, that HTTP transport is correctness-sensitive enough to acquire rather than own; and language metadata is synced from linguist-languages rather than hand-maintained. (4) The product's own output respects a reader's attention better than the repo's internal documentation does: rendered host prompts are 19-370 lines with one clear task, absolute paths, an explicit stop condition and the exact next command. The generalizable lesson across all four groups: every place this project achieved elegance did so by finding the PARAMETER that made two things one (a level count, a record accessor, an adjacency direction, a confidence weight), and every place it did not, it added a table and a test to keep two things agreeing. The former is available in each of DR-011, DR-012, DR-015, DR-023 and DR-024. Two residual nits worth folding into any touch of these files: the remediate fileIntegrity side hand-doubles the sync/async axis four times, and the two sides return the same record shape under different field names.

themes.title: Observational Contract Assessment: Untrusted Producer Execution & Boundary Bypasses
themes.root_cause: The runtime architecture fails to enforce strict execution boundaries, allowing untrusted producer inputs (audited repo code, repo-root binaries, attached git flags, and LLM-authored strings) to execute with host privileges.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Isolate dependency resolution to version-keyed tool caches, enforce bare allowlisted binary tokens with path verification, fence untrusted target-repo text in non-forgeable data envelopes, and mandate pinned releases for external analyzers.

themes.title: Conceptual Design Critique: Governance Hypertrophy & Unpriced Complexity
themes.root_cause: A foundational philosophy treating complexity as zero-cost generated ~17.5k lines of untyped governance scripts and invasive user-facing friction gates while core operational pathways remain unbudgeted and unverified.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Re-establish complexity as a formal design cost in decision gates, consolidate doc-linting into single declarative scripts, bring enforcement scripts under typechecking, and reorder intake gates so repo analysis precedes configuration.

themes.title: Observational Contract Assessment: Weak Verification & Synthetic Grounding Deficits
themes.root_cause: Verification mechanisms (grounding, anchor confirmation, write-scope enforcement) validate syntactic existence or model self-reports rather than semantic correctness, allowing empty quotes or model predicates to launder unverified claims.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Mandate distinctive quote spans matched against cited line ranges, prevent model-chosen predicates from overriding tier-1 grounding failures, stamp verified reviewer identities on artifacts, and enforce strict worktree write-confinement.

themes.title: Observational Contract Assessment: Unpinned Scope Continuity & Concurrency Risk
themes.root_cause: The continuity model lacks run-level git SHA pinning to prevent staleness cascades during long runs, while state persistence primitives rely on unsafe full-object overrides without TOCTOU or concurrency locks.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Pin target repository revisions at run initialization, enforce bidirectional DAG-to-registry consistency in contract tests, replace saveState with lock-held atomic mutation primitives, and validate performance on external benchmark repositories.

themes.title: Conceptual Design Critique: Unbounded Report Aggregation & Hidden Degradation
themes.root_cause: The reporting design lacks per-lens yield caps and finding aggregation, allowing thousands of low-severity maintainability observations to drown critical risks in a 1.29 MB deliverable while parser failures remain undisclosed.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Adopt standard SARIF ingestion, roll up multi-site pattern instances into aggregated findings, budget the human-facing report to executive summaries and top risks, and explicitly disclose parse-tier degradations in report metadata.

themes.title: Observational Contract Assessment: Test Suite Decay & Vacuous Verification
themes.root_cause: Contract test suites rely on local re-implementations, unasserted setup conditions, or retired directory paths, producing false-green suite passes that mask underlying runtime defects.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Refactor test suites to exercise actual production code paths rather than local copies, add cross-platform CI matrix testing, fail loudly on setup step errors, and update path invariants to match current project layouts.

executive_summary: The audit reveals 1,567 findings across the codebase, exposing a tension between conceptual design assumptions and observational contract realities. Conceptual design flaws—specifically a zero-cost complexity posture and unbudgeted report synthesis—have created ~17.5k lines of untyped governance machinery while overwhelming deliverables with single-lens maintainability noise. Concurrently, observational contract assessments surfaced critical vulnerabilities in execution sandboxing, quote grounding, state concurrency, and test suite fidelity that undermine the system's core trust guarantees.
top_risks: Arbitrary code execution on auditor host via untrusted repository imports, root binary shadowing, attached git short-flag bypasses, and un-sandboxed shell commands.
False-confidence verification where single-character quote matches or model-authored predicates mark ungrounded or hallucinated claims as adversarially verified.
Silent execution drift and invalidation cascades caused by unpinned working trees during long-running audit sessions.
State loss and race conditions in remediation workflows due to non-atomic state overrides (saveState) lacking TOCTOU protection.
Governance lock and maintainability drag caused by ~17.5k lines of untyped, fragile enforcement scripts blocking core usability and CI reliability.
